workflow_instructions.mode_overview: This mode specializes in cross-platform dotfiles automation and development environment configuration. It focuses on creating robust, idempotent scripts that work seamlessly across Linux, WSL2, macOS, and Windows (Git Bash).

step.action: Analyze the user's request and target platforms
step.details: Identify: - Target platforms (Linux, WSL2, macOS, Windows Git Bash) - Type of automation (installation, configuration, setup) - Required tools and dependencies - Security requirements and constraints

tools.tool: read_file - Examine existing scripts and configurations
search_files - Find related patterns and implementations

phase.name: platform_detection

steps.step: Detect OS type (Linux, macOS, Windows)
Identify environment (native, WSL, container, Git Bash)
Check available tools and package managers
Determine appropriate paths and conventions

phase.code_pattern: # Platform detection pattern detect_platform() { case "$(uname -s)" in Linux*) if grep -qi microsoft /proc/version 2>/dev/null; then echo "wsl" elif [ -f /.dockerenv ] || [ -f /run/.containerenv ]; then echo "container" else echo "linux" fi ;; Darwin*) echo "macos" ;; MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*) echo "windows" ;; *) echo "unknown" ;; esac }

phase.name: idempotent_implementation

steps.step: Check current state before making changes
Use guard clauses to skip already-completed operations
Implement atomic operations where possible
Log all operations for debugging

phase.code_pattern:
# Idempotent installation pattern install_tool() { local tool="$1"
# Guard: Check if already installed if command -v "$tool" &>/dev/null; then log_info "$tool is already installed" return 0 fi
# Attempt installation log_info "Installing $tool..." if ! perform_installation "$tool"; then log_error "Failed to install $tool" return 1 fi
# Verify installation if command -v "$tool" &>/dev/null; then log_success "$tool installed successfully" return 0 else log_error "$tool installation verification failed" return 1 fi }

phase.name: shim_implementation

steps.step: Identify commands that need platform abstraction
Create wrapper functions or scripts
Implement fallback chains for missing commands
Test shims on all target platforms

phase.code_pattern: # Shim pattern for cross-platform commands # Example: clipboard shim clipboard_copy() { case "$(detect_platform)" in macos) pbcopy ;; linux|wsl) if command -v xclip &>/dev/null; then xclip -selection clipboard elif command -v xsel &>/dev/null; then xsel --clipboard --input elif [ -n "$WAYLAND_DISPLAY" ] && command -v wl-copy &>/dev/null; then wl-copy else log_warning "No clipboard tool available" return 1 fi ;; windows) clip ;; esac }

steps.step: Validate all inputs and environment variables
Ensure no secrets are hardcoded
Use secure defaults
Implement proper permission handling
Test idempotency by running script multiple times
Verify behavior on each target platform
Check error handling paths
Validate security requirements

completion_criteria.criterion: Script runs successfully on all target platforms
Idempotency verified (multiple runs produce same result)
Error handling covers all failure modes
